record.paper_title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About How Causal Set Theory Can Help with Open Questions in Cosmology, but Were Afraid to Ask
record.original_question: Can horizon molecules, defined as linked causal set elements crossing a horizon, be formulated so that counting them yields finite and universal horizon entropy in higher-dimensional spacetimes and for null as well as spacelike hypersurfaces?

evidence.quote: These horizon molecules consist of linked elements with at least one element inside the horizon and at least one outside it.
It turns out that even in the causal set case one does not always obtain a finite number of any kind of horizon molecule, but there will be a finite number of particular kinds of horizon molecules.
Difficulties arising from extending the above simple case to higher dimensions led to the consideration of other kinds of horizon molecules.
However, they needed to require that Σ is strictly spacelike rather than spacelike or null. Ref. 69 showed that there are subtleties in the null case that spoil some of the encouraging results.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. A causal set is a locally finite partially ordered set $(C,\preceq)$, thought of as a discrete model of spacetime in which $x\preceq y$ encodes a causal relation. A causal set $C$ is said to approximate (or be sprinkled into) a Lorentzian manifold $(M,g)$ when its elements arise from a Poisson process on $M$ of density $1/\ell^d$ (where $\ell$ is a fundamental discreteness scale and $d=\dim M$), with the induced order being the causal order of $(M,g)$.

Fix a $d$-dimensional globally hyperbolic Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g)$ containing a causal horizon $H$ (the boundary of the causal past of future null infinity, or any causal horizon analogue) and a hypersurface $\Sigma$ that crosses $H$. Two elements $x,y\in C$ are said to be linked if $x\prec y$ and there is no $z\in C$ with $x\prec z\prec y$.

A horizon molecule, in the most basic form, is a pair (or more generally a finite tuple) of linked elements of $C$ such that at least one element lies inside the horizon (to the future side / interior of $H$) and at least one lies outside it, with the elements lying close to $\Sigma\cap H$ in a precise sense to be specified by the definition.

Problem. Provide a definition of a class of "horizon molecules" — finite configurations of linked causal set elements straddling the horizon $H$ near its intersection with $\Sigma$ — such that all of the following hold simultaneously:

(a) For every dimension $d\ge 2$, the expected number of such molecules in a Poisson sprinkling of $(M,g)$ at density $1/\ell^d$ is finite.

(b) In the continuum limit $\ell\to 0$, this expected count is asymptotic to $\alpha_d\,A(\Sigma\cap H)/\ell^{d-2}$, where $A(\Sigma\cap H)$ is the $(d-2)$-dimensional area of the horizon cross-section and $\alpha_d$ is a universal (geometry-independent) constant depending only on the dimension $d$.

(c) The same definition, with the same universal constants $\alpha_d$, works whether $\Sigma$ is spacelike or null, and the leading-order count remains local to $\Sigma\cap H$ in the null case as well as in the spacelike case.

Does such a definition exist? If yes, exhibit one; if no, prove an obstruction.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Machet–Wang, arXiv:2012.06212, and a 2023 follow-up arXiv:2307.04150) proposes definitions of horizon molecules that give a finite count proportional to horizon area in any dimension, with a dimension-dependent universal constant, for spacelike Σ. However, the extension to null Σ has been shown to fail to yield an entropy local to the horizon–hypersurface intersection in the curved-spacetime continuum limit. Thus the spacelike, higher-dimensional case is partially resolved while the null case remains problematic.

status_evidence.title: On the horizon entropy of a causal set
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a new definition of horizon molecules applying for any causal horizon and its intersection with any spacelike hypersurface; expected count behaves as horizon area times a dimension-dependent factor.
status_evidence.claim: Spacelike, higher-dimensional case is largely resolved with a universal dimension-dependent constant.

status_evidence.title: On Horizon Molecules and Entropy in Causal Sets
status_evidence.snippet: Extends horizon molecules to a null hypersurface crossing the horizon, but the extension fails to yield an entropy local to the hypersurface–horizon intersection in the continuum limit on curved spacetimes.
status_evidence.claim: Null case extension does not produce a local horizon entropy in curved spacetime, so the problem is not fully resolved for null Σ.
